references.text: God formed man from the dust of the ground – the direct background for 'for you were taken from it' in Gen 3:19.
Elihu describes that if God took back His spirit, all flesh would perish and man would return to dust – a direct parallel to the judgment in Gen 3:19.
The psalm reflects on human mortality: God causes man to return to dust, in accordance with the judgment pronounced in Genesis.
'You take away their breath, they die and return to their dust' – a direct parallel to humanity's return to dust.
Ecclesiastes states that all is from dust and all returns to dust – a direct reflection on Gen 3:19.
'The dust returns to the earth as it was' – Ecclesiastes refers directly back to the creation account and the judgment in Gen 3:19.
Paul discusses the contrast between the earthly man of dust and the heavenly one, pointing back to humanity's origin from the ground.
'If anyone will not work, let him not eat' – reflects the principle of the necessity of labor stated in Gen 3:19.
Contrast between dust as a symbol of life and fruitfulness (descendants) and dust as a symbol of death.
Contrast between bread that must be eaten with sweat (the consequence of sin) and bread given in blessing (messianic hope).
